procedures.title: Clear Area Cat A Landing Procedure
procedures.html:
Clear Area Cat A Landing Procedure

Landing Decision Point (LDP)

Height50 ft (15 m) ALS
Airspeed40 KIAS
Rate of DescentLess than 350 ft/min
Note

Radio altimeter heights are shown in the flight path profiles. Refer to Barometric altimeter when obstacles are present in the Landing flight path.

Approach and Landing Procedure

CAUTION

If this procedure is modified, it may not be possible, if an engine fails in the landing path, to carry out a safe OEI landing or achieve the scheduled OEI performance.

  1. Pre-landing checks — Complete.
  2. EDCU, MISC, AURAL INHIBIT — Select NORMAL or LOW HT as required.
    3. Note

    When descending below 150 ft Rad Alt height a vocal message ‘ONE FIFTY FEET’ is activated regardless of the landing gear status. This message is suppressed if AWG is set to LOW HT.

  3. PARK BRAKE — Confirm released.
  4. Initial point — Stabilize the aircraft on final approach course at 300 ft (91.4m) ALS/70 KIAS.
  5. Descend — At 300 ft initiate a descent and a deceleration to pass through LDP with a rate of descent of less than 350 fpm.
  6. Collective/Cyclic Control — At 50ft initiate a flare rotating nose up to achieve a hover at 6ft ALS or to perform a running landing. Maximum nose up attitude at touchdown 15°.
  7. Landing — After Touchdown, centralize controls and reduce collective to MPOG.
  8. Braking — Apply wheel brakes as required.
  9. POST LANDING CHECKS. See page 187. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: CLEAR AREA TAKE-OFF PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
CLEAR AREA TAKE-OFF PROCEDURE

Take‑Off Decision Point (TDP)
Height20 ft (6 m) ATS
Ground speed35 KTS GS
Take-Off
Figure NP 3: Take-Off Profile Clear Area
Note

Radio altimeter heights are shown in the flight path profiles. Refer to Barometric altimeter when obstacles are present in the Take‑Off flight path.

CAUTION

If this procedure is modified, it may not be possible, if an engine fails in the Take‑Off path, to carry out a safe OEI landing or achieve the scheduled OEI performance.

Perform as follows:
1.PARK BRAKE
— Release. Confirm PARK BRK ON advisory not illuminated on CAS.
2.Pilot Altimeter
— Set.
3.Rad Alt
— Check.
4.Power checks
— Carry out as required in accordance with ENGINE POWER CHECKS procedure in Basic RFM Section 4.
5.Nosewheel steering
— LOCK.
6.Engine/Rotor
— TQ/ITT matched as required and check NF/NR 103%.
7.MFD PWR PLANT page
— Check all parameters within normal operating limits and cross‑check with PFD.
8.Warnings and Cautions
— None/as required.
9.Flight controls
— Check correct functioning.
10.Hover
— Establish a 6 ft (1.8 m) ATS hover and note pitch attitude. No winds from rear sectors (090° to 270°).
11.PI/NR
— Note PI value and confirm NR in PLUS Mode.
12.Collective/Cyclic control
— Apply Cyclic to rotate 10° nose down with respect to hover attitude and apply collective to increase hover PI by 5–10% to maintain height. Maintain pitch attitude until airspeed indication starts to increase then reduce pitch down by 5° to climb and start climb to TDP.
13.Take‑Off Decision Point (TDP)
— At TDP continue climb and accelerate to VTOSS (45 KIAS). From VTOSS continue climb and accelerate to VY.
14.Acceleration/Climb
— Passing through VTOSS (45 KIAS) continue acceleration to VY and climb to 1000 ft (300 m) ATS.
15.Landing gear
— Up (when reaching VY but not below 200 ft ATS).
16.AFTER TAKE‑OFF checks
— Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: ENGINE RE-LIGHT (IN FLIGHT)
procedures.html:
ENGINE RE-LIGHT (IN FLIGHT)

If an engine flames out and/or is shut down during flight and if there is no indication of a mechanical malfunction or engine fire, the engine may be restarted. In flight, only one restart attempt is available.

CAUTION
Failure to follow the aborted engine restart procedure may cause damage to the engine.
Engine starting malfunctions are most likely to occur during the engine acceleration cycle to IDLE speed. Monitor engine start and if any of the following occurs:
  • No light‑up within 10 seconds of ENG MODE knob to IDLE
  • ITT increases beyond engine limits
  • ITT invalid (shows X or blank)
  • Engine hangs (NG stagnation below 60%)
  • Starter fails to disengage by 54% NG
Aborted engine restart — carry out:
  1. ENG MODE knob — OFF.
  2. FUEL ENG SOV (EDCU, FUEL page) — CLOSE.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN IN EMERGENCY
procedures.html:
ENGINE SHUTDOWN IN EMERGENCY

Use this procedure to shut down an engine promptly when required by an emergency or malfunction.

CAUTION
Failure to follow the aborted engine restart procedure may cause damage to the engine.
Monitor engine indications. If any of the following occur, shut down the engine:
  • No light‑up within 10 seconds of ENG MODE knob to IDLE
  • ITT increases beyond engine limits
  • ITT invalid (X or blank)
  • Engine hangs (NG stagnation below 60%)
  • Starter fails to disengage by 54% NG
Shut down engine as follows:
  1. ENG MODE knob — OFF.
  2. FUEL ENG SOV (EDCU, FUEL page) — CLOSE.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: CAT A OEI contingency procedures
procedures.html:
AW169 Enhanced Performance

CAT A OEI contingency procedures

EP-specific training summary extracted from the AW169 QRH EP. Use the official QRH/RFM as the controlling source.

Clear Area — engine failure before TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 227
  1. Adjust collective to stop climb and establish descent; adjust pitch attitude to reduce speed.
  2. Perform a running landing, increasing collective to cushion touchdown; maximum nose-up attitude at touchdown 15°.
  3. After touchdown centralize cyclic, lower collective to MPOG, apply wheel brakes as required.
  4. On affected engine, carry out ENGINE SHUTDOWN IN EMERGENCY; consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

Clear Area — engine failure at/after TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 228
  1. Continue acceleration, using collective to maintain NR close to 93%; accelerate to VTOSS 45 KIAS and start climb.
  2. At VTOSS adjust pitch to maintain speed; after positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR.
  3. Continue climb to 200 ft ATS using 2.5 min power, then accelerate to VY using 2.5 min power.
  4. Reduce to continuous OEI power (148% PI) before expiry of 2.5 min power; select landing gear UP when reaching VY.
  5. At 1000 ft ATS, shut down affected engine, complete AFTER TAKE-OFF checks and refer SINGLE ENGINE PROCEDURE.

Landing approach — engine failure before LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 229
  1. Apply collective to set 2.5 min power and maintain NR close to 93%; adjust pitch to accelerate to VBLSS 45 KIAS.
  2. At VBLSS with positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR and climb to 200 ft ALS using 2.5 min power.
  3. At 200 ft ALS, accelerate to VY using 2.5 min power and continue climb toward 1000 ft ATS.
  4. Reduce to continuous OEI power (148% PI) before expiry of 2.5 min power; gear UP when reaching VY but not below 200 ft ATS.
  5. At 1000 ft ALS, shut down affected engine, complete AFTER TAKE-OFF checks and refer SINGLE ENGINE PROCEDURE.

Clear Area — engine failure at/after LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 230
  1. Adjust collective to continue descent; adjust pitch attitude as required to reduce speed.
  2. Perform a running landing, increasing collective to cushion touchdown; maximum nose-up attitude at touchdown 15°.
  3. After touchdown centralize cyclic, lower collective to MPOG, then shut down the affected engine.
  4. Set PARK BRAKE as required, complete POST LANDING CHECKS and consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

G&E H/H — engine failure recognized in hover

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 231
  1. Maintain collective setting or lower collective slightly if required to land.
  2. Increase collective to cushion touchdown; maximum permitted ground speed at touchdown is 5 kt.
  3. After touchdown centralize cyclic and simultaneously reduce collective to MPOG.
  4. Shut down the affected engine and set PARK BRAKE as required.

G&E H/H Variable TDP — engine failure before/at TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 232
  1. Adjust collective to stop climb and establish descent, maintaining rotor speed close to 100% NR.
  2. Maintain the centre of the helipad in sight between yaw pedals as the aircraft descends.
  3. At approximately 10–5 ft ATS, increase collective to cushion landing; maximum allowed GS at touchdown is 5 kt.
  4. After touchdown centralize cyclic, lower collective to MPOG, shut down the affected engine and set PARK BRAKE as required.
  5. Consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

G&E H/H Variable TDP — engine failure at/after TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc pp. 233–234
  1. Rotate pitch down to -15°; maintain until 15 kt GS, then rotate nose-up to level attitude for 1 second.
  2. After 1 second continue rotation to 5° nose-up and accelerate to VTOSS 45 KIAS; maintain NR close to 93%.
  3. At VTOSS maintain speed; after positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR.
  4. Continue climb to 200 ft ATS or TDP height +90 ft ATS using 2.5 min power.
  5. At 200 ft ATS or TDP height +105 ft ATS, whichever is higher, accelerate to VY and continue to 1000 ft ATS.
  6. Reduce to continuous OEI power (148% PI) before expiry of 2.5 min power; gear UP at VY, release PARK BRAKE, then shut down the failed engine at 1000 ft ATS.

G&E H/H Variable LDP — engine failure before LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc pp. 235–236
  1. Rotate pitch down to -15°; maintain until 15 kt GS, then rotate nose-up to level attitude for 1 second.
  2. Continue rotation to 5° nose-up and accelerate to VBLSS 45 KIAS; maintain NR close to 93%.
  3. At VBLSS with positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR.
  4. Continue climb to 200 ft ALS or LDP height +70 ft ALS using 2.5 min power.
  5. At 200 ft ALS or LDP height +70 ft ALS, whichever is higher, accelerate to VY and continue toward 1000 ft.
  6. Reduce to continuous OEI power (148% PI), gear UP at VY, release PARK BRAKE and shut down the failed engine at 1000 ft ALS.

G&E H/H Variable LDP — engine failure at/after LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 237
  1. Adjust collective to establish descent, maintaining rotor speed close to 100% NR.
  2. Adjust pitch attitude to keep the centre of the helipad between the pilot's ankles.
  3. At approximately 10–5 ft ALS, increase collective to cushion landing; maximum allowed GS at touchdown is 5 kt.
  4. After touchdown centralize cyclic, lower collective to MPOG, shut down the failed engine and set PARK BRAKE as required.
  5. Consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

Offshore / Elevated Helideck — engine failure recognized in hover

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 238
  1. Maintain collective setting or lower collective slightly if required to land.
  2. Increase collective to cushion landing as touchdown becomes imminent; maximum permitted GS at touchdown is 5 kt.
  3. After touchdown centralize cyclic and simultaneously reduce collective to MPOG.
  4. Shut down the affected engine and consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

Offshore / Elevated Helideck — engine failure before TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 239
  1. Adjust collective to establish descent and maintain rotor speed approximately 100% NR.
  2. Maintain aircraft position over the take-off point while descending.
  3. At approximately 10–5 ft ATS, increase collective to cushion landing; maximum allowed GS at touchdown is 5 kt.
  4. After touchdown centralize cyclic and simultaneously reduce collective to MPOG.
  5. Shut down the affected engine and consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.

Offshore / Elevated Helideck — engine failure at/after TDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc pp. 240–241
  1. Continue rotation to 12° nose-down to achieve 15 kt GS, using collective to maintain NR close to 93%.
  2. Increase attitude to 6° nose-up and continue acceleration to VTOSS; after positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR.
  3. At VTOSS 45 KIAS, maintain speed and climb to 200 ft ATS using OEI 2.5 min power.
  4. At 200 ft ATS, select landing gear UP while accelerating to VY using OEI 2.5 min power.
  5. Continue climb to 1000 ft ATS or cruise level, reducing to continuous OEI power (148% PI) before 2.5 min power expires.
  6. Release PARK BRAKE, shut down the affected engine at 1000 ft ATS, complete AFTER TAKE-OFF checks, select PFD MAG and refer SINGLE ENGINE PROCEDURE.

Offshore / Elevated Helideck — engine failure before LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc pp. 244–245
  1. Apply collective to set OEI 2.5 min power and maintain NR close to 93%; set pitch 10° nose-down from present attitude to accelerate to VBLSS 45 KIAS.
  2. At VBLSS with positive climb, lower collective to recover 101% NR and continue climb to 200 ft ALS using OEI 2.5 min power.
  3. At 200 ft ALS, select landing gear UP while accelerating to VY using OEI 2.5 min power.
  4. Continue to 1000 ft ALS or cruise level, reducing to continuous OEI power (148% PI) before 2.5 min power expires.
  5. Release PARK BRAKE, shut down the failed engine, complete AFTER TAKE-OFF checks, select PFD MAG and refer SINGLE ENGINE PROCEDURE.

Offshore / Elevated Helideck — engine failure at/after LDP

AW169 QRH EP Emerg-Malfunc p. 246
  1. Adjust collective to continue descent while reducing rate of descent; adjust pitch attitude as required to reduce speed.
  2. At approximately 15–10 ft ATS, increase collective to cushion landing; maximum nose-up attitude at touchdown 15° and maximum GS 5 kt.
  3. After touchdown centralize cyclic and reduce collective to MPOG.
  4. Set PARK BRAKE as required, shut down the affected engine and consider EMERGENCY GROUND EGRESS.
AW169 EP training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: GROUND AND ELEVATED HELIPORT / HELIDECK VARIABLE TDP PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
GROUND AND ELEVATED HELIPORT / HELIDECK VARIABLE TDP PROCEDURE

CAUTION

If this procedure is modified, it may not be possible, if an engine fails in the Take-Off path, to carry out a safe OEI landing or achieve the scheduled OEI performance.

  1. Pilot Altimeter — Set 0 ft or nearest 1000 ft (300 m) setting to T-O altitude, with collective at MPOG.
  2. Rad Alt — Check
  3. Power checks — Carry out as required in accordance with ENGINE POWER CHECKS procedure in Basic RFM Section 4.
  4. NOSEWHEEL lock — LOCK
  5. PARK BRAKE — As required
  6. Engine/Rotor — TQ/ITT matched as required and check NF/NR 103%.
  7. MFD PWR PLANT page — Check all parameters within normal operating limits and cross check with PFD.
  1. Warnings and Cautions — None/as required.
  2. Flight controls — Check correct functioning.
  3. Landing lights — For night operations set as follows:
    • Flying pilot side set pointing down;
    • Non flying pilot side set pointing forward.
  4. Hover — Establish a 6 ft (1.8 m) ATS hover and note pitch attitude and PI. No winds from rear sectors (090° to 270°).
  5. Collective/Cyclic Control — Increase collective to start a slow climb (max 300 fpm) to TDP (max 400 ft) maintaining the centre of the helipad in sight between yaw pedals.
  6. Take-Off Decision Point (TDP) — Rotate in 2 sec. 15 deg. nose down with respect to hover attitude using collective to maintain height. Maintain this attitude until airspeed indications starts to increase, then reduce pitch down by 5 deg. to accelerate through VTOSS (45 KIAS). From VTOSS continue climb and accelerate to Vy.
  7. Acceleration/Climb — Passing through VTOSS (45 KIAS) continue acceleration to Vy and climb to 1000 ft (300 m) ATS.
  8. Landing gear — UP (when reaching Vy but not below 200 ft (60 m) ATS).
  9. AFTER TAKE-OFF checks. See page 183. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: GROUND AND ELEVATED HELIPORT / HELIDECK VERTICAL PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
GROUND AND ELEVATED HELIPORT / HELIDECK VERTICAL PROCEDURE

Take-Off Decision Point Height (TDP)
TDP50 ft (15 m) ATS
Continued Take-Off Heights
Minimum height during CTO15 ft ATS (5 m ATS)
Note

Radar Altimeter heights are shown in the flight path profiles. Refer to Barometric altimeter for Elevated Heliport/Helideck operations.

Figure NP 2: Take-Off Profile Vertical Heliport Procedure

CAUTION

If this procedure is modified, it may not be possible, if an engine fails in the Take-Off path, to carry out a safe OEI landing or achieve the scheduled OEI performance.

  1. Pilot Altimeter — Set 0 ft or nearest 1000 ft (300 m) setting to T-O altitude, with collective at MPOG.
  2. Rad Alt — Check.
  3. Power checks — Carry out as required in accordance with ENGINE POWER CHECKS procedure in Basic RFM Section 4.
  4. NOSEWHEEL lock — LOCK.
  5. PARK BRAKE — As required.
  6. Engine/Rotor — TQ/ITT matched as required and check NF/NR 103%.
  7. MFD PWR PLANT page — Check all parameters within normal operating limits and cross check with PFD.
  1. Warnings and Cautions — None/as required.
  2. Flight controls — Check correct functioning.
  3. Landing lights — For night operations set as follows:
    • Flying pilot side set pointing down;
    • Non flying pilot side set pointing forward.
  4. Hover — Establish a 6 ft (1.8 m) ATS hover and note pitch attitude and PI. No winds from rear sectors (090° to 270°).
  5. Collective/Cyclic Control — Increase PI by 20–25% in 2 sec. to climb to TDP (50 ft ATS) maintaining hover position.
  6. Take-Off Decision Point (TDP) — Rotate in 2 sec. 15° nose down with respect to hover attitude. Maintain this attitude until airspeed indications start to increase, then reduce pitch down by 5° to accelerate through VTOSS (45 KIAS). From VTOSScontinue climb and accelerate to VY.
  7. Acceleration/Climb — Passing through VTOSS (45 KIAS) continue acceleration to VY and climb to 1000 ft (300 m) ATS.
  8. Landing gear — UP (when reaching VY but not below 200 ft (60 m) ATS).
  9. AFTER TAKE-OFF checks. See page 183. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: GROUND OR ELEVATED HELIPAD APPROACH AND LANDING VARIABLE LDP PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
GROUND OR ELEVATED HELIPAD APPROACH AND LANDING VARIABLE LDP PROCEDURE

Approach and Landing Procedure

CAUTION

If this procedure is modified, it may not be possible, if an engine fails in the landing path, to carry out a safe OEI landing or achieve the scheduled OEI performance.

  1. Pre-landing checks — Complete.
  2. Landing direction — If possible orientate the aircraft for an approach into the prevailing wind.
  3. Landing lights — For night operations set as follows:
    • Flying pilot side set pointing down;
    • Non flying pilot side set pointing forward.
  4. EDCU, MISC, AURAL INHIBIT — Select NORMAL or LOW HT as required.
    5. Note

    When descending below 150 ft Rad Alt height a vocal message ‘ONE FIFTY FEET’ is activated regardless of the landing gear status. This message is suppressed if AWG is set to LOW HT.

  5. Initial point — Establish an approach at 20 kts GS and 50 ft higher than LDP height and slow down maintaining height to reach a hover with the centre of helipad in sight between the yaw pedals.
  6. Descent to landing surface — Start descending with no more than 300 fpm maintaining the centre of helipad in sight between the yaw pedals to reach a 6 ft hover above landing surface.
  7. Landing — After touchdown, centralize cyclic and reduce collective to MPOG.
  8. PARK BRAKE — As required after landing.
  9. POST LANDING CHECKS. See page 187. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: OFFSHORE / ELEVATED HELIDECK APPROACH AND NORMAL LANDING PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
OFFSHORE / ELEVATED HELIDECK APPROACH AND NORMAL LANDING PROCEDURE

Landing decision point (LDP)

Height30 ft ALS
Groundspeed12 kts

Procedure

  1. Pre-landing checks — Complete.
  2. Landing direction — If possible carry out an approach into the prevailing wind.
  3. Landing lights — For night operations set as follows: Flying pilot side set pointing down; Non flying pilot side set pointing forward.
  4. EDCU, MISC, AURAL INHIBIT — Select NORMAL or LOW HT as required.

Note

When descending below 150 ft Rad Alt height a vocal message ‘ONE FIFTY FEET’ is activated regardless of the landing gear status. This message is suppressed if AWG is set to LOW HT.

  1. PARK BRAKE — Apply, Confirm pressure can be felt on brake pedals and PARK BRK ON advisory illuminated on CAS.
  2. PFD menu — Select DG as required.
  3. Initial point — Establish a constant descent with a ROD of 200 and 300 fpm and decelerate slowly towards the LDP (30 ft ALS at 12 kts GS and position the deck at 45°) maintaining the flight path to keep the rotor tip path plane outboard, but close to the edge of the helideck.
  4. LDP — The LDP is positioned with the aircraft approximately 45° from the centre of the helideck viewed through the lower part of the windscreen.
  5. Landing — When passing LDP fly directly to landing position, flare to reduce ROD and speed to achieve HIGE over landing position.
  6. Touchdown — When over the landing position descend vertically and use collective to cushion touchdown. Maximum nose up attitude at touchdown 15°. Maximum GS at touchdown 5 kts (9 km/hr).
  7. PARK BRAKE — As required after landing.
  8. POST LANDING CHECKS — See page 187. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.

procedures.title: OFFSHORE / ELEVATED HELIDECK TAKE-OFF NORMAL PROCEDURE
procedures.html:
OFFSHORE / ELEVATED HELIDECK TAKE-OFF NORMAL PROCEDURE

  1. ECS — As required.
  2. Pilot Altimeter — Set 0 ft or nearest 1000 ft (300 m) setting to T-O altitude, with collective at MPOG.
  3. Rad Alt — Check.
  4. Power checks — Carry out as required in accordance with ENGINE POWER CHECKS procedure in Basic RFM Section 4.
  5. NOSEWHEEL lock — LOCK.
  6. PARK BRAKE — Apply. Confirm pressure can be felt on brake pedals and PARK BRK ON advisory illuminated on CAS.
  7. Engine/Rotor — Check TQ matched and NF/NR 103%.
  8. MFD PWR PLANT page — Check all parameters within normal operating limits and cross check with PFD.
  9. PFD menu — Select DG on Rig, Otherwise check heading and select as required.
  10. Warnings and Cautions — None/as required.
  11. Landing Lights — For night operations set as follows:
    • Flying pilot side set pointing down
    • Non flying pilot side set pointing forward.
  12. Hover — Establish a 5 ft (1.5 m) ATS hover with the helicopter nose wheel positioned approximately 2 m from the front edge of the helideck and note hovering PI.
Note

If wind is from right sector, it is recommended that the aircraft is oriented to minimize the crosswind.

  1. Collective/Cyclic Control — Increase PI by 15% in approximately 2 sec. to climb vertically at 400 fpm or greater, maintaining hover position.
  2. Take-Off Decision Point (TDP) — At 25 ft (7.5 m) ATS rotate nose to 12° nose down to achieve 15 kts GS then rotate to 6° nose up while continuing to accelerate to VY (75 KIAS).
  3. VY — Above 200 ft, Landing Gear UP.
  4. PARK BRAKE — Release. Confirm PARK BRK ON advisory extinguishes on CAS.
  5. PFD menu — Select MAG as required.
  6. AFTER TAKE-OFF checks. See page 183. — Complete.
AW169 training reference. For training use only.
